features.label: Grenada (France)
features.source: French Grenada before cession to Britain at the Treaty of Paris.

features.label: Dominica (France)
features.source: France claimed Dominica before Britain acquired it at the Treaty of Paris; the island's Kalinago population remained autonomous in much of the interior.

features.label: Saint Lucia (France)
features.source: French Saint Lucia before the Treaty of Paris.

features.label: Saint Vincent (France)
features.source: French Saint Vincent before Britain acquired the island at the Treaty of Paris.

features.name: New France
features.label: New France
features.source: Champlain's habitation at Quebec and the river below it: Cliopatria puts New France at about 1,600 km² of mainland at its 1609 slice.

features.name: New France
features.label: New France
features.source: Trois-Rivières and the first Acadian settlements around the Bay of Fundy; about 17,000 km² across the two in Cliopatria's 1632 slice.

features.name: New France
features.label: New France
features.source: Ville-Marie founded at Montreal, joining the settled river from Montreal to the Saguenay; about 25,000 km² in 1642.

features.name: New France
features.label: New France
features.source: New France made a royal province, with the first posts west toward the Great Lakes; about 48,000 km² by 1673.

features.name: New France
features.label: New France
features.source: The pays d'en haut around lakes Huron and Michigan; about 66,000 km² in 1683 and 87,000 by 1713.

features.name: New France
features.label: New France
features.source: Utrecht cost France Acadia, Newfoundland and the Hudson Bay claims, which is why the Fundy shape ends here; the western posts to Lake Superior kept growing, to about 141,000 km² with Louisiana by 1757.

features.name: New France
features.label: Louisiana (France)
features.source: The lower Mississippi from the Gulf to the Missouri, drawn with the part that follows the river's west bank rather than the whole later Purchase, which is only what Spain takes over in 1763. Cliopatria has the valley at about 52,000 km² of settled ground inside a claim this size.

features.label: French Guiana
features.source: French Guiana has remained French, apart from the short Portuguese occupation during the Napoleonic wars, which this map does not split out.

features.label: Saint-Domingue (France)
features.source: The richest colony in the Caribbean, lost to the Haitian Revolution.

features.label: Santo Domingo (France)
features.source: Ceded by Spain at Basel and retaken by Spain after the Napoleonic wars reached the island.

features.label: Louisiana (France)
features.source: Retroceded by Spain at San Ildefonso and sold to the United States three years later.

features.label: French Antilles
features.source: Martinique and Guadeloupe were settled in 1635; the later Saint-Barthélemy and Saint-Martin holdings are drawn with them from the same date.

features.label: Falkland Islands (France)
features.source: France established Port Louis in February 1764 and gave the settlement up to Spain; Britain's Port Egmont on the far side of the islands is too brief and too small to draw separately.
